llm.summary: Jensen Huang's resignation is now fact, not rumor, and the AI complex is repricing a leadership/governance discount on top of an already-deteriorating capex narrative: NVDA is tumbling, Nebius fell ~10-14% on weak guidance and higher 2026 capex, CoreWeave sank ~10%, and Asian AI names slipped while Chinese chipmakers rallied. The macro vise tightened again — CPI came in hot, a Fed official called it 'borderline disturbing,' December hike odds are near 100%, the 10-year is back above 5% and the dollar hit a 19-month high. Hard assets broke: gold lost $4,000 and is at ~$3,973 with $3,870 the next support, bitcoin slid toward $72-74k, confirming that real rates, not geopolitics, are in control. Notably, European equities hit a record high even as Asia and US futures fell — the rotation out of US AI concentration is going somewhere, not into cash. Flows corroborate: Technology at -78, Health Care 96, Staples 92, Real Estate 82, Materials 81, Value now leading Growth by 121 points (widened from 111 yesterday). Beneath the Nvidia noise, the physical layer of AI keeps compounding: Meta is funding seven gas plants for its largest data center, China is attacking the global gas-turbine market, and Türkiye-Canada signed a CANDU assessment deal. Politics is converting the Nvidia scandal into a durable policy risk — Democratic senators demanding export records, Cotton pushing to ban CXMT — which raises the floor under domestic semicap and reshoring. Today's tape hinges on AMAT (gapping +6.1% into earnings) and CSCO as the clean read on whether AI capex is actually slowing or just losing its spokesman.

market_thesis.short_term: Risk-off with a specific address: US mega-cap AI. The Huang resignation removes the single most effective narrative anchor the sector had, and it lands on a tape where the 10-year is above 5% and a December hike is nearly fully priced — multiple compression and a credibility shock at the same time. Expect continued dispersion rather than a broad drawdown: European equities at records, small caps turning positive, and Value +121 over Growth say capital is rotating, not fleeing. Gold below $4,000 and bitcoin under $74k mean there is currently no hedge that works except short duration and cash-generative value. AMAT and CSCO tonight are the swing factor: a strong AMAT print with solid orders decouples the physical AI buildout from the Nvidia governance story and stabilizes semicap; a miss or soft orders validates the Nebius/CoreWeave capex-digestion read and the selloff broadens.
market_thesis.medium_term: Reflation (33.9, +11.2) and Stagflation (33.1, +13.1) are effectively tied with Goldilocks collapsing to 16.7 (-13.8) — a central bank hiking into an economy that is not breaking but whose consumer is fraying. That argues for higher-for-longer nominal yields, a firm dollar, continued multiple compression on long-duration narrative assets, and sustained rotation into Health Care, Staples, Real Estate, Materials and Financials. Inside AI the dividing line sharpens from 'chips vs everything' to 'contracted electrons, turbines, fabs and permits vs storytelling and leveraged credit': Meta financing seven gas plants, China attacking gas turbines, CoreWeave courting the credit markets, Nebius raising capex while pushing revenue into 2027. Export-control legislation following the Nvidia case is the mechanism that converts a scandal into a durable earnings impairment for China-exposed semis and a durable subsidy for US fabs. Anthropic's IPO plus SpaceX's remain the capital-absorption events that drain incremental dollars from incumbent AI megacaps and force index reconstitution.
market_thesis.long_term: Energy, permits, political consent and capital access are the binding constraints on AI, and the economics accrue to owners of generation, turbines, grid hardware, copper, gas and nuclear fuel rather than to owners of the narrative. The Huang episode makes explicit that a trillion-dollar capital cycle was partly underwritten by one person's credibility — institutionalizing that cycle means slower, more contested, more expensive buildout and a permanently higher risk premium on single-key-man AI equities. AI leadership is now a national-security variable, embedding duplicated supply chains, export-control friction and a higher structural inflation floor. For households, affordability — electricity, insurance, groceries, mortgages at 5%+ yields — is the dominant variable, entrenching value retail, generics and distribution, managed care, insurance and essential services over undifferentiated discretionary. Market structure keeps concentrating global capital in US listings even as the AI leadership inside those listings churns.

short_term: Investors are selling the AI narrative premium while keeping the AI physical exposure — Chinese chipmakers rallied and European equities hit records on the same day Nvidia fell, so the money is rotating by geography and by layer of the stack, not de-risking wholesale.

Households are losing their inflation hedges simultaneously: gold below $4,000 and bitcoin under $74k mean savers get no protection from either, pushing demand toward short-duration cash and money-market yield at 5%.

Consumers keep spending but show strain (CNBC/NRF monitor) — trading down in groceries and discretionary while holding onto experiences; Park Hotels cut guidance, suggesting the premium-lodging end is cracking first.
Homebuyers are stalling again as the 10-year reclaims 5%; mortgage demand concentrates in 15-year and jumbo niches where rates slid, and 'housing market crash' is a rising search query.
Workers are feeling pay lag inflation (Boston Globe), which drives second-job, side-income and value-channel behavior rather than aggregate spending collapse.
Public attention is pouring into AI data centers (+149% vs base) with local, concrete queries — water usage, 'near me' — the early signature of NIMBY resistance rather than enthusiasm.
long_term: Security and trust become priced attributes of technology: the Nvidia espionage case, AI firms hiring ex-intelligence operatives and data-breach search interest mean customers will pay for provenance, auditability and domestic supply.

Energy becomes a consumer-visible cost of the AI era; residents will increasingly vote on data-center siting, water and electricity rates, slowing buildout and advantaging incumbents with existing permits and generation.
Affordability-first consumption persists as a regime, not a cycle — value retail, generics, distribution and insurance take permanent share from mid-market discretionary.
People want health span and self-directed care: GLP-1 attention stays elevated, telehealth (HIMS gapping +8.8%) and continuous-monitoring devices keep converting episodic care into subscription care.

Capital formation moves to mega private listings (Anthropic, SpaceX) and tokenized venues launching without Big Tech's approval — retail wants access to private-market returns and 24-hour venues, reshaping where price discovery happens.
Geographic diversification of equity exposure returns after a decade of US concentration; European records during a US AI shock will be remembered by allocators.
